question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III) delivered a gross return of 22.4% over FY24. The CRISIL AIF Cat III Index (peer benchmark) returned 14.6% and the Nifty 50 TRI returned 28.9% over the same period. Fund expenses were 2.2% and carry was 3.5%. On a post-expense, pre-carry, pre-tax basis (benchmark-reporting convention), what is the fund's relative return vs the CRISIL AIF Cat III Index?

explanation.text: The Logic: Post-expense, pre-carry return = Gross - Expenses = 22.4% - 2.2% = 20.2%. Relative return vs CRISIL AIF Cat III = 20.2% - 14.6% = +5.6 percentage points (outperformance). Carry of 3.5% is not deducted because the benchmark-reporting convention for Cat III is post-expense, pre-carry, pre-tax. Nifty 50 TRI (28.9%) is a distractor — the relevant peer benchmark per SEBI is the CRISIL AIF Cat III index, not a broad-market index. The Trap: Option A (+1.2) subtracts both expenses and carry first. Option C (-8.7) uses Nifty 50 TRI as the benchmark — it is not the correct peer benchmark for a Cat III fund. Option B (+7.8) is the gross-of-expenses relative figure — inconsistent with SEBI's post-expense convention. Note: Pages 223-225 of the workbook set the post-expense, pre-carry, pre-tax reporting convention for Cat III and provide the CRISIL AIF Cat III benchmark as the reference example.
